headline: Committee approves amendments to accessory dwelling bill, discusses Molokaʻi B&B cap

meeting.body: Maui County Council Housing and Land Use Committee
meeting.voteItem: Chair's amendment on rural zoning and accessory dwelling parking
meeting.summary: Members approved two amendments to the bill on accessory dwelling units, each with seven ayes. The county must adopt its rules by December 31, 2026. The committee also took up a bill capping Molokaʻi bed and breakfast homes at five.
meeting.recap: The first bill updates county rules to follow a state law on accessory dwelling units (small extra homes).[[0:06:05]] Planning staff said that state law allows two accessory dwelling units on each residential lot.[[0:06:23]] Planning staff said the county must adopt its rules by December 31, 2026.[[0:06:29]] All three planning commissions recommended approval, with 13 changes from the Planning Department.[[0:14:37]] A fire captain said the fire department may revisit its second-access road rule as more homes are allowed.[[0:32:14]] Members approved a revised version of the bill and a council member's amendment on conditional zoning agreements, with seven ayes.[[1:02:32]] A second amendment on rural lots and parking passed with seven ayes.[[1:03:10]] The second bill would cap bed and breakfast homes on Molokaʻi at five and keep them 1,000 feet apart.[[1:11:30]] The committee deferred the bill without objection.[[1:42:49]]
decided: Members approved an amendment on rural lot rules and parking language.
meeting.next: The committee chair will keep working on the workforce housing tax bill with the Finance and Housing departments. A fire captain said a future fire code change may revisit the second-access requirement.

moments.q: Fire captain: second access rule to be revisited "especially in light of what happened in Lahaina"
"I resent the state for eroding our home rule authority regarding land use and zoning."
Testifier: without the homeowner rate, taxes can go up "by three times, sometimes even more"

Cap on bed and breakfast homes on Molokaʻi

issues.oneLine: The committee is updating county rules so residential lots can have two accessory dwelling units, as a state law requires.
issues.why: Planning staff said the county general plan encourages more housing through accessory dwellings.

deadlines.t: County must adopt an ordinance to comply with the state accessory dwelling law.

issues.next: The county must adopt its accessory dwelling ordinance by December 31, 2026.
issues.brief: Planning staff said building permits are sent to the water and wastewater departments to check that service is adequate.[[#1]] Planning staff said subdivision rules (CC&Rs) that restrict accessory dwellings still win over the state law.[[#2]] Planning staff said current accessory dwelling units cannot be used as short-term or vacation rentals.[[#3]]
